logline: A 70-year-old retired postal worker pursues his lifelong dream of learning ballet alongside a struggling young dancer, each discovering what it means to keep moving forward.

seasons.review_body: Navillera aired on tvN from March to April 2021 and averaged 3% nationwide cable viewership, consistently topping its time slot. Based on the acclaimed Daum webtoon, the series pairs two actors of radically different generations - Park In-hwan as the 70-year-old dreamer Shim Deok-chul and Song Kang as the young dancer Lee Chae-rok - and asks them to sustain a mentor-student relationship of genuine depth across 12 episodes. Critics responded to the show's refusal to manufacture drama: the conflicts arise from Deok-chul's early-stage dementia and Chae-rok's financial precarity, not from plot contrivances. The ballet sequences were praised for authenticity, and the second half's emotional weight was described as earned rather than manipulative. IMDb settled at 8.7 on a substantial vote count.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Navillera Season 1 Episode 1 aired March 22, 2021 on tvN as the premiere of a 12-episode limited series that averaged 3 percent nationwide cable viewership and consistently topped its time slot. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. Kdrama Kisses called it 'such a heartfelt drama - an inspirational story of two people at very different points pursuing their dreams.' The episode establishes the central contrast economically: a 70-year-old retired postal worker who has waited his whole life to dance, and a 23-year-old who dances but cannot afford to keep doing so. Director Han Dong-hwa builds character through motion rather than backstory. Park In-hwan's Shim Deok-chul and Song Kang's Lee Chae-rok are established as a mentor-student pairing of genuine depth from the first episode.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The first episode establishes the central contrast economically: a 70-year-old man who has waited his whole life to dance, and a 23-year-old who dances but cannot afford to keep doing so. Director Han Dong-hwa wastes no time on backstory that can be discovered in motion.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Deok-chul watches a ballet performance through a studio window, and the distance between longing and action collapses in a single held shot.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.review_body: Navillera Season 1 Episode 12 aired April 27, 2021 on tvN as the finale of a 12-episode limited series that averaged 3 percent nationwide cable viewership. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. Kdrama Kisses called the show an 'inspirational story of two people at very different points pursuing their dreams.' The finale delivers on the central promise without false resolution: Deok-chul's early-stage dementia and Chae-rok's financial precarity arrive at meaningful endpoints that honor the show's honest treatment of aging, illness, and the cost of chasing a dream late in life. Critics who praised the series for avoiding manufactured drama found the finale's restraint consistent with the emotional register maintained across 12 episodes. The final ballet sequence is the payoff of an arc that began with an old man watching through glass.
